sections.title: Graphing and Elimination
sections.learning_target: Students will solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
i_cans: I can construct graphical representations of systems and connect intersection points to solutions.
I can use elimination to solve systems and interpret the solution type.
I can determine whether a system has one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions from algebraic and graphical evidence.

spiral.Intro: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
spiral.Review: Graph linear functions and interpret key features.
spiral.Mastery: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.

sections.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
sections.learning_target: Students will solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
i_cans: I can formulate a substitution plan when one equation is already written in an efficient form.
I can apply substitution to solve systems and interpret the ordered-pair solution.
I can assess which algebraic method is more efficient for a given system.

spiral.Intro: Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
spiral.Review: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
spiral.Mastery: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.

sections.title: Writing and Solving Systems from Situations
sections.learning_target: Students will create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
i_cans: I can build a system of equations that represents two constraints in a situation.
I can predict the meaning of a solution before solving from the context and variables.
I can design a solution pathway that connects equations, calculations, and a contextual conclusion.

spiral.Intro: Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
spiral.Review: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
spiral.Mastery: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.

sections.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities
sections.learning_target: Students will graph and interpret linear inequalities.
i_cans: I can construct a boundary line and shaded region for a linear inequality.
I can use test points to interpret which region satisfies an inequality.
I can critique a graph of a linear inequality using the boundary, shading, and solution region.

spiral.Review: Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
spiral.Mastery: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.

sections.title: Linear Systems of Inequalities
sections.learning_target: Students will analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
i_cans: I can formulate a system of inequalities that represents multiple constraints.
I can extend graphing strategies to represent overlapping solution regions.
I can apply feasible-region reasoning to interpret possible solutions in context.

spiral.Intro: Analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
spiral.Review: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.
spiral.Mastery: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
